stories.headline: US rule closes chip 'remote access' loophole, adds license curbs on 4 Southeast Asian nations and Brazil

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 16, 2026, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule on remote access to advanced 'super intelligence' chips and servers, written by and at the direction of Treasury and the National Security Council, so export restrictions cannot be circumvented through data centers in third countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) released an interim final rule (IFR)—written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council—to address remote access to advanced super intelligence (SI) chips and servers.

key_facts.fact: A license is now required to ship advanced chips to any data center in the world that provides more than 12 million 'aggregate TPP' of compute to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other Country Group D:5 destinations; the rule also tightens requirements on foundries and packagers and formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule.
key_facts.excerpt: ...if the exporter... has 'knowledge'... that the item is destined to a data center anywhere in the world that provides or will provide access to more than 12 million 'aggregate TPP'... tightens the rules for chip foundries and packagers, and formally rescinds the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule.

key_facts.fact: Shipments of advanced AI chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil now need licenses, with an exemption for US-headquartered buyers such as AWS, Google and Microsoft that file monthly reports.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the new rules, companies will need licences to export, re-export or transfer certain advanced American AI chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil. There is an exemption for chips destined for companies headquartered in the US...

key_facts.fact: The rule is expected to be published and take effect on Nov. 19; data centers already serving Chinese firms get 90 days from the effective date to obtain a license, and comments are due 60 days after publication.
key_facts.excerpt: BIS has indicated that the IFR is expected to be formally published and go into effect on November 19... must obtain a license within 90 days of the effective date of this rule

key_facts.fact: Singapore's digital and trade ministries said they were 'studying the details of this new measure carefully' and engaging affected companies and US authorities; until Nov. 16 it was not illegal for such data centers to serve Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent.
key_facts.excerpt: "We are studying the details of this new measure carefully," said a joint media statement by the Ministry of Digital Development and Information and the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry... Until the US government acted on Nov 16, it was not illegal for these data centres to provide computing power to Chinese tech giants like Alibaba, ByteDance and Tencent.

key_facts.fact: CFR senior fellow Chris McGuire said that if enforced, the rules would effectively end the business of neoclouds such as Singapore-based Megaspeed; the rule lands ahead of the Nov. 19 Trump-Xi meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR), said that if the rules are enforced, "the business of neocloud companies such as Singapore-based Megaspeed... will effectively be over."

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has warned customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act could expose them and Nvidia to US legal action, and said it will not sell chips to customers renting more than 50% of their GPUs to Chinese companies, CNBC reported on Nov. 17 citing sources.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia warned customers that a new law could expose them and the chipmaker to "legal action" over Chinese access to chip capacity... Nvidia said it would not sell its chips to customers who rent more than 50% of the graphics processing units... to Chinese companies.

stories.headline: Nvidia board creates export-control oversight committee; board not weighing Huang's return

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 17, Nvidia's board established a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee for board-level oversight of national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk; its National Security and Global Trade Compliance teams will report to it and to interim CEO Colette Kress.
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA's existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the Committee and to Interim CEO, Colette Kress, on day-to-day operations.

key_facts.fact: The committee is chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson, with directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri, meets at least quarterly and will retain independent outside experts in law, national security and trade compliance.
key_facts.excerpt: The Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will also include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly

key_facts.fact: Board chairman Harvey Jones said advanced silicon and 'the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security'.
key_facts.excerpt: "NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security..." said Harvey Jones, Chairman of NVIDIA's Board of Directors.

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 16, CNBC reported that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO and is focused on a probe led by Wachtell Lipton into whether his conduct compromised national security or company secrets.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on Monday he 'wouldn't mind' seeing Huang return; a petition to reinstate him had over 185,000 signatures, including 9,300 Nvidia employees.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump on Monday said that he "wouldn't mind" seeing Huang return to the helm, and a petition to reinstate Huang had gathered over 185,000 signatures as of Monday lunchtime, including 9,300 Nvidia employees.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia director of developer technology Nader Khalil wrote to the 10 board members and Huang's roughly 60 direct reports warning that 'irreplaceable talent' was contemplating leaving if Huang is not reinstated, the WSJ reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Nvidia Director of Developer Tech Nader Khalil wrote to the board arguing that not reinstating Jensen Huang could cost Nvidia "irreplaceable talent"... a group that included Huang's roughly 60 direct reports as well as the 10 members of the board

stories.headline: Commerce and DOJ say Megaspeed export probe began in 2024; Nvidia blacklisted it in June 2025

key_facts.fact: In a joint statement dated Nov. 16, the Commerce and Justice departments said Commerce opened an investigation into Singapore's Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations, citing a need to 'address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting'.
key_facts.excerpt: ...the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations.

key_facts.fact: Commerce requested records from Nvidia on sales to Megaspeed in May 2025; Nvidia put Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list in June 2025, when BIS agents with Singaporean police ran an on-site end-use check and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.
key_facts.excerpt: In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia... In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its "no sell" list... conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.

key_facts.fact: The Justice Department now leads a criminal investigation; no charges have been announced and Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department now leads a criminal investigation. No charges have been announced in the case, and Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.

key_facts.fact: CFR's Chris McGuire called the statement 'very, very strange', saying it does not explain why Commerce did not cut Megaspeed off from chips, since it kept buying after Nvidia's no-sell listing.
key_facts.excerpt: "Very, very strange statement tonight... about Megaspeed. The facts here just don't add up, and this does nothing to explain why Commerce did not cut Megaspeed off from chips."

key_facts.fact: Chinese records show Alice Huang's husband Kang Wei built a state-backed data center network in China with proposed investments exceeding $9 billion between 2021 and 2024, the WSJ reported.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese records: Alice Huang's husband Kang Wei built a state-backed data center network in China, with proposed investments exceeding $9B between 2021 and 2024

stories.headline: Nvidia reports Q3 today, its first results since Huang's exit, with the stock down ~24% this month

key_facts.fact: Nvidia will release fiscal Q3 2027 results (quarter ended Oct. 25) at about 1:20 p.m. PT on Nov. 17, with the earnings call at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET).
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA will host a conference call on Tuesday, November 17, at 2 p.m. PT (5 p.m. ET) to discuss its financial results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2027, which ended October 25, 2026... results are publicly announced at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT.

key_facts.fact: It is the first report since Jensen Huang resigned; interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress will present. Nvidia had guided Q3 revenue of about $108 billion, roughly 90% growth year on year, and has topped its own forecast for 14 straight quarters.
key_facts.excerpt: The chipmaker's revenue has topped the upper end of its own forecasts for 14 straight quarters... In August, the company forecast third-quarter revenue of about $108bn (€98bn), an increase of about 90% from a year earlier.

key_facts.fact: FactSet consensus expects revenue of $108.9 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.47; shares fell 4.1% to $156.14 on Monday.
key_facts.excerpt: Wall Street expects Nvidia to post financial third-quarter revenue of US$108.9 billion, up about 91 per cent from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings of US$2.47 a share... Nvidia shares fell 4.1 per cent to US$156.14 on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Options price a 7.8% move either way after the report; shares trade at under 11 times forward earnings, the lowest multiple since 2013, and have fallen 35% from the Oct. 6 high.
key_facts.excerpt: The options market is pricing in a 7.8% move for the shares in either direction... trading at less than 11 times earnings estimated over the next 12 months, their lowest multiple since 2013.

key_facts.fact: Ahead of the report, Korea's Kospi closed below 5,000 for the first time in nine months (down 2.59%) and Taiwan's Taiex fell 2.31% after a 6.03% plunge on Monday; Nvidia is down almost 24% this month.
key_facts.excerpt: Kospi fell 2.59% to 4,968.48 on Nov. 17, a nine-month low... Taiex dropped 2.31% to 40,092.11 after Monday's 6.03% plunge... Nvidia is down almost 24% this month

key_facts.fact: Investors will watch whether Kress slows Nvidia's tens of billions in investments in customers and suppliers, and whether the gross margin still falls to 71-72% in Q4 as memory costs rise.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia forecast a third-quarter margin of 74%... and expected it to fall further to 71–72% in the fourth... Investors will be looking for signs that Kress might slow those investments.

stories.headline: Nvidia unveils Rubin HPC, a science GPU with a record 50,000+ CUDA cores, due in 2028

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced Rubin HPC at the SC26 supercomputing conference on Nov. 16, a new GPU in the Vera Rubin platform aimed at simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics.
key_facts.excerpt: Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows.

key_facts.fact: The chip has more than 50,000 CUDA cores, a record for a single Nvidia GPU, plus sparse-data acceleration and seventh-generation NVLink; it is expected in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability... seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink... Rubin HPC is expected to be available in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Today's Rubin GPU has 28,672 CUDA cores, so Rubin HPC likely needs a multi-die (possibly four-die) package; Nvidia gave no HBM capacity or bandwidth figures.
key_facts.excerpt: Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package... Nvidia didn't share any details of the Rubin HPC GPU's HBM capacity or bandwidth

key_facts.fact: HPCwire describes the chip, with 3x the vector cores of Blackwell, as a recommitment to FP64 double-precision math after Nvidia stopped increasing it in its last two data center GPU generations.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia today unveiled the Rubin HPC, a new GPU that features 3X the vector cores of Blackwell. The chip shows a recommitment to FP64 on Nvidia's part after abandoning increases in double-precision 64-bit floating point math in its last two generation of data center GPUs.

key_facts.fact: Ian Buck, Nvidia's VP of hyperscale and HPC, framed it around AI agents: 'For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery.'
key_facts.excerpt: "For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery," said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA.

stories.headline: Google signs first commercial superhot-rock geothermal deal: 50 MW from Quaise for Oregon data centers

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 17, Quaise Energy announced Google signed a power purchase agreement for 50 MW of superhot geothermal power from Project Obsidian in Central Oregon, starting as early as 2030, to support Google's data centers in The Dalles.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has signed a power purchase agreement (PPA) for 50 megawatts (MW) of superhot geothermal power from Project Obsidian... slated to support Google's existing data center operations in The Dalles, Ore... Beginning as early as 2030

key_facts.fact: OPB calls it the world's first commercial-scale superhot rock geothermal deal, and Quaise's first commercial agreement; the companies did not disclose the price.
key_facts.excerpt: A Texas-based geothermal company has inked the world's first commercial-scale superhot rock geothermal energy deal with Google... The companies did not disclose the sale price... The partnership with Google is Quaise's first commercial geothermal agreement.

key_facts.fact: The deal is worth more than $500 million according to the WSJ, for a plant Quaise says will cost about $350 million.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal is worth more than $500m, Benoît Morenne reported for the Wall Street Journal. Quaise told the newspaper the project will cost about $350m.

key_facts.fact: Phase one uses conventional drilling; phase two is expected to be the world's first use of millimeter-wave drilling, which vaporizes rock with a gyrotron, a technology not yet proven at commercial scale.
key_facts.excerpt: The second phase is expected to be the first in the world to use millimeter wave drilling... then bring in a gyrotron, a device that fires millimeter-wave energy at the rock, vaporizing it... The technology is still unproven at commercial scale.

key_facts.fact: Superhot geothermal can produce up to 10x more power per well than conventional geothermal, Quaise says; CEO Carlos Araque estimates Project Obsidian could reach about 1 GW within a decade.
key_facts.excerpt: He estimates Project Obsidian could generate about one gigawatt of energy, enough to power about one million homes, in the next decade.

stories.headline: TOP500 adds just 27 new supercomputers, a record low, as hardware flows to AI factories

key_facts.fact: The 68th TOP500 list, released Nov. 16 at SC26 in Chicago, contains only 27 new systems (5.4% of the list), the lowest new-system turnover in the list's history.
key_facts.excerpt: The November list contains only 27 new systems, representing 5.4 percent of the TOP500. This is the lowest level of new-system turnover in the history of the list

key_facts.fact: The top 10 is unchanged since June: China's LineShine stays No. 1 at 2.198 exaflop/s, ahead of El Capitan (1.809), Frontier (1.353), Aurora (1.012) and JUPITER Booster (1.000).
key_facts.excerpt: LineShine remains No. 1 with 2.198 Exaflop/s... El Capitan follows at No. 2 with 1.809 Exaflop/s, ahead of Frontier at 1.353 Exaflop/s, Aurora at 1.012 Exaflop/s, and JUPITER Booster at 1.000 Exaflop/s.

key_facts.fact: TOP500 attributes the slowdown to growth shifting to AI factories: citing Epoch AI, five US hyperscalers owned about 71% of global AI compute as of Q4 2025, and cumulative AI compute exceeds the equivalent of 15 million H100 GPUs.
key_facts.excerpt: cumulative global AI compute has surpassed the equivalent of 15 million NVIDIA H100 GPUs. As of the fourth quarter of 2025, five major U.S. hyperscalers owned an estimated 71 percent of global AI compute... growth has indeed shifted toward AI factories

key_facts.fact: The largest newcomer is South Korea's HANGANG at KISTI, No. 12 with 342.6 petaflop/s; the entry threshold rose 7.3% to 2.857 petaflop/s.
key_facts.excerpt: HANGANG, installed at the KISTI Supercomputing Center in South Korea, is the highest-ranked new system at No. 12... The No. 500 system now delivers 2.857 Petaflop/s, up 7.3 percent

key_facts.fact: LineShine is a CPU-only system built on custom LX2 processors with the proprietary LingQi interconnect.
key_facts.excerpt: The CPU-only system runs on custom LX2 processors connected by the proprietary LingQi interconnect.
